**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your
projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists i

ts eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body
`{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`details`

is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked
, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `AUT
H_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` c
arries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is vali
d but not allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different M
CPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n| `
NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this wr
ite — a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `FE
ATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests —
see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 504

| The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New

error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

#

## Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts

a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUTH_
REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, a
nd\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`** (
the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge`

field (`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIR
ED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server you
rself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpja

m.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up t

o **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-va

riables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exce

eded. Slow down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned

during the preview.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-
After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather tha
n a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs\nyour backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may

not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playg

round — under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

**Catalog** — discover the IDs everything else takes:

| Endpoint | What it does

|
| - | - |
| `GET /me` | The account behind the key |
| `GET /organizations` | The organizations the caller belongs to — where
`organizationId` comes from. A key is bound to one organization and only ever sees that one |\n| `GET /projects` | Projects the k
ey can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers` | The project's saved MCP servers |\n| `GET
/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions` | A server's stored revisions, newest first: captures of its tools and server
info, recorded whenever they change (`?limit=&cursor=`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNum
ber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to
store, so they are unknown, not absent |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What
changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values.
A field listed in `droppedFields.from` or `droppedFields.to` was not stored on that side, so a change to it is unknown |\n| `GET /
projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |\n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/c
lients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |\n| `GET`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /projects/{projectId}/clients/{c
lient}` | Read, edit, or delete a client. The path segment takes a client **name or ID** |\n| `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients/
{client}/servers` | Replace the client's server attachments (a replacement — omitted servers are detached) |\n| `POST /projects/{p
rojectId}/clients/{client}/duplicate` | Copy a client's current config into a new client |\n| `GET /chat-sessions` | Chat sessions

(`?projectId=&status=&limit=&before=`) |

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
stand
alone server group, optionally pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval\nsuites and goals run against. Reads need project memb
ership; **every write\nneeds project admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read\nback as `expectedRevision`

, and a stale value returns `CONFLICT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |\
n| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or cre
ate one |\n| `GET`, `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to
clear `serverAttachmentId`, `skillSelection`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |\n| `GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/
resolve` | Preview the host config, closed server set, and pinned plugin versions this environment resolves to right now |\n| `POS
T /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |\n| `PO
ST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |\n\nArchive and restore are expl
icit sub-actions rather than a `DELETE` because the\nrow is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops\n
plugin pins whose version no longer exists.\n\n**Server diagnostics & primitives** (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`

):

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../validate` | Connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot |
|
`POST .../doctor` | Full health workflow: probe → connect → initialize → capabilities |\n| `POST .../check-oauth` | Does this serv
er require an OAuth grant? |\n| `POST .../tools` | List the server's tools |\n| `POST .../tools/call` | Execute a tool; returns th
e MCP `CallToolResult` plus additive `durationMs`, and `authChallenge` when the result asks for sign-in (see [Sign-in challenges](
#sign-in-challenges)) |\n| `POST .../prompts` | List the server's prompts |\n| `POST .../prompts/get` | Render a prompt; returns t
he MCP `GetPromptResult` verbatim |\n| `POST .../resources` | List the server's resources |\n| `POST .../resources/read` | Read on
